Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Nur (The Light), because the word "light" (al-nur) is repeated seven times in it, and because it includes the parable of God's light, through which He guides to faith and the Qur'an, and this is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an.

The Aims of the Surah

• Explaining a set of the legal rulings related to fornication (al-zina), slander (al-qadhf), and li'an (the oath of mutual cursing between spouses).

• Mentioning the innocence of 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, of what the people of hypocrisy accused her of, and of those who joined them in spreading that talk, in the incident of the slander (hadith al-ifk). It also contains a severe warning for those who love to spread indecency among the believing men and women, and an explanation that their leader toward indecency and wrongdoing is Satan, along with a warning against falling into his snares.

• Mentioning the means of protection from falling into the crime of fornication. It explains the etiquette and rulings for entering inhabited and uninhabited houses, such as seeking permission (al-istidhan) and greeting (al-salam), and explains the times at which those who live together in one house should seek permission. It also contains the command to lower the gaze, to cover adornment, and to guard the private parts, as well as the command to chastity (al-'afaf) and marriage (al-nikah), in order to protect honour and lineage, and the prohibition of prostitution (al-baghaʾ), which was widespread in the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance), and the encouragement to marry off the unmarried (al-ayama) and the slaves (al-mamalik).

• Discussing the purest places on earth, which are the mosques, and describing the hearts of their people who have been illuminated by the light of God Most High, in a parable presented with the utmost eloquence and clarity; and presenting a parable for the misguidance of disbelief and explaining the state of one who falls into it.

• Describing the greatness of God Most High and the wondrous nature of His creation, and the favours He bestows upon people; explaining God's dominion and His management of this universe, His wisdom in the varieties of His creation, His power, and His knowledge of all that.

• Censuring the conditions of the hypocrites and pointing out the evil of their inner intentions toward the Prophet ﷺ, contrasting this with the condition of the believers and God's promise to them of succession (al-istikhlaf) upon the land in return for obedience.

• The command to obey the Prophet, and a warning and threat against disobeying him, by explaining the fate of those who disobey, and explaining the etiquette to be observed with the Prophet in addressing him and when mentioning him.

[Al-Tafsir]

This is a great surah of the Qur'an which We have sent down, and We have made obligatory the acting upon its rulings, and We have sent down within it clear proofs, so that you may take heed, O believers, through these clear verses, and act upon them.

The fornicatress and the fornicator, the unmarried ones among them: the punishment for each of them is one hundred lashes with a whip. The Sunnah has established, in addition to this flogging, exile (al-taghrib) for a period of one year. Do not let compassion for them lead you to abandon the punishment or to lighten it, if you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day and act in accordance with the rulings of Islam. And let a group of the believers witness the punishment, as a means of public disgrace, deterrence, admonition, and taking a lesson.

The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist woman who does not acknowledge the prohibition of adultery; and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist man who does not acknowledge the prohibition of adultery. As for the chaste men and the chaste women, they do not accept that, and that marriage has been forbidden to the believers. This is clear evidence for the prohibition of marrying an adulteress until she repents, and likewise the prohibition of marrying off an adulterer until he repents.

Those who accuse chaste women and men of unlawful sexual conduct, without bringing four upright witnesses to support the accusation, shall be flogged with eighty lashes. Their testimony shall never be accepted. Those are the ones who have departed from obedience to Allah.
But those who repent after that, make amends, and rectify their conduct, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful towards them, and accepts their repentance.

Those who accuse their wives of adultery, and have no witnesses to support their accusation other than themselves, then each of them must testify before the judge four times, saying: "I testify by God that I am telling the truth about what I accused her of, namely adultery." In the fifth testimony he adds an invocation against himself, that he deserves the curse of God if he is lying in what he says.

Those who accuse their wives of adultery, and have no witnesses to support their accusation other than themselves, then each of them must testify before the judge four times, saying: "I testify by God that I am telling the truth about what I accused her of, namely adultery." In the fifth testimony he adds an invocation against himself, that he deserves the curse of God if he is lying in what he says.

Through his testimony, the wife becomes liable to the punishment for adultery, which is stoning to death. She can avert this punishment only by swearing against his testimony four oaths, by God, that he is lying in his accusation of her with adultery, and by adding to the fifth testimony an invocation upon herself of the wrath of God, if her husband was truthful in his accusation against her. In this case, the two are separated (the procedure of li'an, mutual cursing).

Through his testimony, the wife becomes liable to the punishment for adultery, which is stoning to death. She can avert this punishment only by swearing against his testimony four oaths, by God, that he is lying in his accusation of her with adultery, and by adding to the fifth testimony an invocation upon herself of the wrath of God, if her husband was truthful in his accusation against her. In this case, the two are separated (the procedure of li'an, mutual cursing).

Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, O believers, in legislating this ruling for spouses, He would have brought upon the liar among the two who invoke curses (on each other) what they called down upon themselves. And (know that) Allah is Oft-Returning (to mercy) toward whoever of His servants repents, and All-Wise in His legislation and His management (of affairs).

Indeed, those who brought the most heinous lie, namely the accusation of Umm al-Mu'minin 'Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) of indecency, are a group among you, O community of Muslims. Do not consider their statement to be evil for you; rather, it is good for you, because it contained the clearing of the Mother of the Believers and her innocence, the making known of her mention, the raising of ranks, the expiation of sins, and the testing of the believers. For every individual who spoke the slander is the recompense of his sin according to what he did; and the one who bore the greater part of it, namely 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the chief of the hypocrites (may Allah curse him), for him is a great punishment in the Hereafter, which is abiding in the lowest level of the Fire.

Why did the believing men and women not think well of one another when they heard that slander, which is the false accusation against them, and say: "This is a clear lie against 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her"?
Why did the accusers not bring four upright witnesses to support their claim? When they failed to do so, those are the liars in the sight of Allah.

Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy to you, by which His kindness encompassed you in your religion and your worldly affairs, so that He did not hasten your punishment, and He accepted the repentance of those among you who repented, you would have been struck, because of what you plunged into, by a tremendous punishment.

When you received it from one another and passed the slander on with your mouths, saying what you had no knowledge of, and it was a false statement, and you had no knowledge of it. These were two prohibited things: speaking falsehood, and saying something without knowledge. You considered it a trivial matter, but it is grave in the sight of Allah. In this there is a strong deterrent against being careless about spreading falsehood.

Why did you not say, when you heard it: "It is not right for us to speak of this; glory be to You, O Lord, this is a tremendous slander" against the wife of Your Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ)? It is a great lie, carrying a heavy burden of sin and deserving of punishment.

"Allah admonishes you that you never return to the like of this (accusation and false charge), if you are believers."

Note: the Qur'anic verse itself is ﴿يَعِظُكُمُ اللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُوا لِمِثْلِهِ أَبَدًا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (24:17).
Allah makes clear to you the verses that contain the legal rulings and the admonitions. Allah is All-Knowing of your actions, and All-Wise in His legislation and His governance.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 19:

Indeed, those who love that indecency spread among the Muslims, through slander of unchastity or any other evil speech about them, will have a painful punishment in this world, by the enforcement of the prescribed penalty (hadd) upon them, and other worldly afflictions. And in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire if they do not repent. And Allah alone knows their lie, and knows the interests of His servants and the outcomes of affairs, while you do not know that.

And were it not for Allah's favor upon those who were involved in the tale of slander (al-ifk), and His mercy toward them, and that Allah is merciful to His believing servants with a vast mercy, both in this world and in the Hereafter, He would not have explained these rulings and admonitions, and He would have hastened punishment upon those who opposed His command.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not follow the paths of Satan. Whoever follows the paths of Satan, he commands him with foul deeds and wicked acts. Were it not for Allah's favor upon the believers and His mercy toward them, not one of them would ever have been purified from the defilement of his sin. But Allah, by His bounty, purifies whom He wills. And Allah is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your intentions and your deeds.

Let not those of virtue among you and of wealth swear to cease giving to their relatives, the poor and the needy who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need, and to the emigrants in the way of Allah, and to withhold support from them because of a sin they committed. Rather, let them pardon and overlook their offense, and not punish them. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? So forgive them. And Allah is All-Forgiving toward His servants, Most Merciful to them. In this is an exhortation to pardon and forgiveness, even when one is met with wrongdoing.

Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unsuspecting, believing women of adultery, women whose hearts never imagined such a thing, are cursed and cast out from the mercy of Allah in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment in the Fire of Hell. In this verse is evidence for the disbelief of whoever reviles or accuses one of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) of wrongdoing.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "The Simplified Exegesis") on surah 24, verse 24:

That punishment will come on the Day of Resurrection, the day when their tongues will testify against them to what they uttered, and their hands and feet will speak of what they did.

In this day, Allah will pay them their full recompense for their deeds with justice, and they will know on that great standing that Allah is the Manifest Truth, who is the Truth, whose promise is true, whose threat is true, and everything from Him is true, the One who does not wrong anyone the weight of an atom.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 24, verse 26:

Every evil man and woman, and every evil utterance and action, is suited to evil and conforms to it. Every good man and woman, and every good utterance and action, is suited to good and conforms to it. The good men and women are cleared of the evil that the wicked hurl at them, and for them there is forgiveness from Allah that encompasses all sins, and a generous provision in Paradise.

O you who have believed, enter not houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants. The wording of this, from the Sunnah, is: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" That seeking of permission is better for you, that you may remember (by doing it) the commands of God, and thus obey Him.

If you find no one in the houses, do not enter them until permission is given to you. And if you are told, "Go back," then go back, and do not insist. Returning is purer for you, for a person has circumstances that he dislikes anyone to see. And Allah is All-Knowing of what you do, and He will recompense every doer for his deed.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 29:

Yet there is no blame upon you for entering, without seeking permission, houses that are not designated as the dwelling of particular people, but are for anyone in need of their benefit, such as the houses prepared as charity for the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil) along the roads of travelers and other such facilities. In them are benefits and needs for whoever enters them, and seeking permission would be a hardship. And Allah knows your apparent and hidden conditions.

Say, [O Prophet], to the believing men that they should lower their gaze from what is not lawful for them of women and of nakedness, and that they should guard their private parts from what Allah has forbidden, such as fornication, sodomy, exposing nakedness, and the like. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do regarding what He commands them and what He forbids them.

And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze from what is not lawful for them of nakedness, guard their private parts from what Allah has forbidden, and not display their adornment to men, but strive to conceal it, except for the outward garments which custom has made usual to wear, provided there is nothing in them that invites temptation through them. And let them cast their head coverings over the openings of their upper garments at the chest, so that their covering may be complete. And let them not display their hidden adornment except to their husbands, for they see from them what others do not see. Some of it, such as the face, the neck, the hands and the forearms, may be seen by their fathers, the fathers of their husbands, their sons, the sons of their husbands, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, the sons of their sisters, their Muslim women (and not non-Muslim women), what their right hands possess of slaves, male attendants who have no desire or need for women, such as the simpleminded who follow others only for food and drink, or young children who have no knowledge of the matters of women's nakedness and in whom desire has not yet arisen. And let women not strike their feet when they walk so as to make heard the sound of what is hidden of their adornment, such as anklets and the like. And return, O believers, to obedience to Allah in what He has commanded you of these beautiful qualities and praiseworthy morals, and abandon what the people of jahiliyyah (the age of pre-Islamic ignorance) were upon of base morals and qualities, in hope that you may succeed in the good of this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 32:

"And marry off, O believers, those among you who are unmarried, both free men and free women, and your righteous male and female slaves. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty. Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 33:

Those who cannot afford marriage due to their poverty or other reasons should keep themselves chaste, abstaining from what Allah has forbidden, until Allah enriches them from His bounty and makes marriage easy for them. As for those slaves who wish to buy their freedom through a contract of manumission (mukatabah) with their masters, in exchange for an amount of money they pay to them, their owners should enter into such a contract with them if they know good in them: sound judgment, the ability to earn, and righteousness in religion. And they should give them some of the money, or remit part of what they were contracted to pay. You are not permitted to compel your slave girls into fornication in pursuit of worldly wealth. How could such a thing occur from you when they desire chastity and you reject it? In this there is the utmost condemnation of your foul deed. As for whoever compels them to fornication, then Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving toward them and Merciful to them, and the sin rests upon the one who compelled them.

And indeed We have sent down to you, O people, verses of the Qur'an as clear proofs upon the truth, and an example from the reports of earlier nations, the believers among them and the disbelievers, and what befell them and what was done to them, which serves as a lesson and an example for you, and an admonition by which those who fear Allah and beware of His punishment may be warned.

God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. He manages the affair in them and guides their inhabitants. He, glorified is He, is Light, and His veil is Light. By Him the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them have been illuminated. The Book of God and His guidance are a light from Him, glorified is He. Were it not for His light, may He be exalted, darkness would have piled up, one layer upon another. The likeness of His light by which He guides to Himself, which is faith and the Qur'an in the heart of the believer, is like a niche (mishkah), which is a recess in the wall that is not a through-opening. In it is a lamp, where the niche gathers the light of the lamp so that it does not scatter. That lamp is in a glass (zujajah) which, because of its clarity, is like a shining star, like a pearl. It is kindled from the oil of a blessed tree, which is the olive tree, neither eastern only, so the sun does not reach it at the end of the day, nor western only, so the sun does not reach it at the beginning of the day, but it stands in a place on the earth midway, neither toward the east nor toward the west. Its oil, because of its purity, nearly gives light of itself before fire touches it. When fire touches it, it lights up with an eloquent illumination: light upon light. It is light from the brilliance of the oil upon light from the kindling of the fire. That is the likeness of guidance shining in the heart of the believer. God guides and grants success in following the Qur'an to whomever He wills, and He strikes the parables for people so that they may understand from Him His parables and His wisdom. God is All-Knowing of everything; nothing is hidden from Him.

This light shines in houses (mosques) that Allah has commanded be raised in status and built, and in which His name is mentioned through the recitation of His Book, glorification (tasbih), proclamation of His oneness (tahlil), and other kinds of remembrance. In them, people glorify Allah morning and evening:

Men whom neither trade nor commerce distracts from the remembrance of God, the establishment of the prayer, and the giving of zakat (obligatory charity) to its rightful recipients. They fear the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which hearts will turn about between hope for deliverance and fear of ruin, and on which eyes will turn about, looking to see what destiny they will face.

So that Allah may reward them for the best of their deeds and increase them from His bounty by multiplying their good deeds. And Allah provides for whomever He wills without account, rather He gives him a reward beyond what his deeds could reach, and without counting or measure.

Those who disbelieve in their Lord and deny His messengers—their deeds, which they thought would benefit them in the Hereafter, such as maintaining the ties of kinship and freeing captives, and others, are like a mirage (sarab), which is what is seen like water on level ground at midday: the thirsty one thinks it is water, but when he reaches it, he finds it is not water. Thus the disbeliever thinks his deeds will benefit him, but when the Day of Resurrection comes, he finds no reward for them, and he finds Allah, glorified and exalted, awaiting him in ambush (bi-l-mirsad), so He pays him back for his deeds in full. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, so let the ignorant not be slow to expect that threat, for it will surely come.

Or [their deeds are] like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by waves, above which are further waves, and above them clouds: darknesses upon darknesses. When one stretches out his hand, he can barely see it. As for the disbelievers, the darknesses of polytheism, misguidance and corrupt deeds have piled up upon them. And whomever Allah does not grant a light from His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet, by which he may be guided, has no guide at all.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 41:

Have you not known, O Messenger, that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, of creatures, and the birds, spreading their wings in the sky? Each one of them knows its prayer and its glorification. Allah is All-Knowing of what each worshipper and glorifier does; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for that.
And to Allah alone belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; to Him belongs authority over them, and to Him is the return on the Day of Resurrection.

Have you not seen that Allah, glorified and exalted, drives the clouds to wherever He wills, then gathers them after they have been scattered, then makes them piled up, so that rain comes forth from within them? And He sends down from the sky, from clouds that resemble mountains in their enormity, hail, striking with it whomever He wills of His servants and turning it away from whomever He wills among them, according to His wisdom and decree. The flash of its lightning within the clouds nearly takes away the sight of those who look at it, because of its intensity.

Among the signs of God's power, glory be to Him, is that He alternates the night and the day, one coming after the other, and their differing in length and shortness. Indeed, in that is a sign by which everyone who has insight takes heed.

Allah the Exalted created every creature that crawls upon the earth from water, so water is the origin of their creation. Among these creatures are those that move on their bellies, crawling like snakes and the like; among them are those that walk on two legs, like humans; and among them are those that walk on four, like cattle and the like. Allah, glorified and exalted, creates whatever He wills, and He is capable of everything.
We have indeed sent down in the Qur'an clear signs that guide to the truth. And Allah guides and grants success to whomever He wills of His servants to the straight path, which is Islam.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 47:

The hypocrites say: "We believe in Allah and in what the Messenger has brought, and we obey their command." Then after that, groups of them turn away and do not accept the ruling of the Messenger. And those are not believers.

And when they are called, in their disputes, to what is in the Book of Allah and to His Messenger, so that he may judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away, refusing to accept the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger, even though it is the truth about which there is no doubt.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 49:

And if the right lies on their side, they come to the Prophet (ﷺ) willingly, submitting to his judgment, because they know that he judges with truth.

What is the cause of their turning away? Is it the sickness of hypocrisy (nifaq) in their hearts, or did they doubt the prophethood (nubuwwah) of Muhammad (ﷺ), or is the cause that they fear Allah's and His Messenger's ruling would be unjust? Never (kalla, a particle of rejection)! They do not fear injustice. Rather, the cause is that they are themselves the wrongdoers, the wicked.

The true believers, however, when they are called to have their disputes judged by the Book of Allah and the ruling of His Messenger, their way is to accept the judgment and say: "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful ones, who attain what they seek in the Gardens of Bliss.

Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger in what they command and forbid, fears the consequences of disobedience, and beware of the punishment of Allah, those are the ones who will attain bliss in Paradise.

The hypocrites swore by Allah with their utmost effort in emphatic oaths: "If you were to order us, O Messenger, to go out for jihad with you, we would surely go out." Say to them: "Do not swear falsely. Your obedience is well known to be only with the tongue. Indeed, Allah is All-Aware of what you do, and He will recompense you for it."

Say, [O Messenger], to the people: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger." But if you turn away, then upon the Messenger is only what he has been commanded to do, which is to convey the message, and upon all of you is what you have been charged with, which is compliance. And if you obey him, you will be guided to the truth. And the Messenger is responsible only for conveying the message of his Lord clearly.

God has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will give them victory, by making them inheritors of the land of the polytheists and making them successors in it, just as He did with their predecessors among the believers in God and His messengers. He will also make their religion, which He has approved for them, namely Islam, a mighty and firmly established religion, and He will change their state from fear to security, provided they worship God alone, remain steadfast in His obedience, and associate nothing with Him. As for whoever disbelieves after that succession, security, establishment, and complete authority, and denies God's blessings, those are the ones who have departed from obedience to God.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 56:

And establish the prayer in its complete form, give zakat to those entitled to it, and obey the Messenger (ﷺ), that perhaps Allah may have mercy upon you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 57:

Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape Allah on earth. Rather, He is able to destroy them, and their return in the Hereafter is to the Fire, and what an evil destination and final abode it is. This is a general directive to the ummah, even though the address in it is to the Messenger (ﷺ).

O you who have believed, let your slaves and those whom your right hands possess, and the children among you who have not yet reached puberty, ask permission (before entering upon you) at three times: before the Fajr prayer, because it is the time of rising from sleeping garments and putting on waking clothes; and at midday, when you remove your clothes for the afternoon rest; and after the 'Isha' prayer, because it is a time for sleep. These three times are times of nakedness (awrah) for you, when covering is reduced. As for other times, there is no blame if they enter without permission, because of their need to come in to you, for they go about attending on you, and because custom has made some of you frequent others at those times to attend to affairs. Thus does Allah make clear to you the rulings on seeking permission; He makes clear to you His signs, His rulings, His proofs, and the laws of His religion. And Allah is All-Knowing of what benefits His creation, All-Wise in His management of their affairs.

When the children among you reach puberty (al-ihtilam) and become responsible for the legal obligations of the Shariah, they must seek permission to enter at all times, just as the adults do. Just as Allah makes clear the etiquette of seeking permission, so Allah, may He be exalted, makes His signs clear to you. And Allah is All-Knowing of what benefits His servants, All-Wise in His legislation.

The elderly women who have no more desire for marriage, and for whom men no longer have desire, there is no blame on them if they lay aside some of their outer garments, such as the cloak worn over their clothing, without displaying adornment or deliberately exposing their beauty. Yet keeping modest covering is better for them. And Allah is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your intentions and deeds.

There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, in leaving off the obligatory duties which they are unable to perform, such as jihad and the like, which depend on the sight of the blind, the soundness of the lame, or the health of the sick. Nor is there any blame upon you, O believers, for eating from your own homes, where your spouses and your children are, and this includes the homes of your children; or from the homes of your fathers, your mothers, your brothers, your sisters, your paternal uncles, your paternal aunts, your maternal uncles, or your maternal aunts; or from homes entrusted to your care in the absence of their owners, with their permission; or from the homes of friends. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. So when you enter homes, whether inhabited or uninhabited, let some of you greet others with the greeting of Islam, which is: "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh" (Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings), or: "As-salamu 'alayna wa 'ala 'ibadillahi as-salihin" (Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah) if there is no one in them. This greeting is one that Allah has prescribed; it is blessed, it increases affection and love, and it is good and pleasing to the hearer. In this manner, Allah makes clear to you the signs of His religion and His verses, so that you may understand them and act upon them.

Indeed, the true believers are those who affirm belief in God and His Messenger and act in accordance with His law. When they are with the Prophet (ﷺ) on a matter that has gathered them for the benefit of the Muslims, none of them departs until he has sought his permission. Indeed, those who seek your permission, O Prophet, are the ones who truly believe in God and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some need of theirs, grant permission to whomever you wish of those who ask leave to depart for an excuse, and ask God's forgiveness for them. Indeed, God is Forgiving toward the sins of His servants who repent, and Merciful toward them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 24, verse 63:

Do not address the Messenger of Allah, when you call him, as you call one another, by saying "O Muhammad" or "O Muhammad son of Abdullah." Rather, honour him and say, "O Prophet of Allah" or "O Messenger of Allah." Allah certainly knows those hypocrites who slip away from the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ secretly, without his permission, seeking shelter with one another. So let those who oppose the command of the Messenger of Allah beware lest a trial or calamity befall them, or a painful, grievous punishment strike them in the Hereafter.

Verily, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, in creation, dominion and worship. His knowledge encompasses all that you are upon, and on the Day when the servants return to Him in the Hereafter, He will inform them of their deeds and recompense them for them. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything; nothing of their deeds and states is hidden from Him.
